Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: Business-to-business payments are supported by NIP as an account-to-account transfer rail usable for corporate payments (collections and disbursements) across participating banks and indirect participants, as described by NIBSS and the SIIPS 2025 case study.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Person-to-business payments are supported through Nigeria’s account-based instant payments ecosystem (NIP) and associated merchant payment solutions (e.g., NQR/merchant collections and bank/fintech rails described in NIBSS and CBN payments materials).

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government payments are supported via digital channels, including tax and government fee payment capabilities that leverage bank transfer rails and online portals; the CBN Payments System Vision 2025 includes digitization of government collections and payments.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: NIP supports person-to-person transfers (“transfers”/instant account-to-account payments) as a core use case and is used widely via bank channels and fintech front-ends, per NIBSS product description and the SIIPS 2025 NIP case study.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is the primary regulator/overseer of payment systems and plays a direct governance role in NIBSS (operator of NIP). Public NIBSS governance information indicates the NIBSS Board is chaired by a CBN Deputy Governor, evidencing strong central-bank governance involvement in national payments infrastructure.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: Nigeria has frequent public performance/statistics reporting on retail payments through NIBSS-published industry statistics (regular updates on e-payments volumes/values across channels) and CBN payments publications; this supports a high score for routine public reporting frequency.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: CBN publishes payment-system regulatory and policy documents (e.g., Payments System Vision) and NIBSS publishes scheme/product information for NIP; however, a single consolidated “scheme rulebook” for NIP is not clearly located in the public sources used, so score reflects substantial public documentation rather than full rulebook transparency.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Nigeria operates a national instant payment rail via Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) called NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP), launched 2011 and described as fully operational and “mature” in the 2025 AfricaNenda SIIPS country case study, supporting 24/7 real-time transfers across a large participant network and very high annual volumes/value (e.g., ~11bn transactions in 2024 in the SIIPS case study).
